## 1. Goal

Create the `Sim` struct and the functions that create a simulation, add jobs to it (before or during a run), reset it and destroy it. Every input is validated before any state changes, and every PRD §5 error code is returned for its trigger. This also settles O-8: what happens to a rejected job.

## 2. Background

**From PRD §4 The Sim struct holds three collections:**

1. **Pending arrivals:** jobs added but not yet arrived, sorted by arrival time. A job added mid-run is inserted here.
2. **Waiting heap:** arrived jobs, ordered by the policy key. For aging, the stored key is the 64-bit integer 1000·b − alpha_milli·r, so it never changes while the job waits.
3. **Running heap:** started jobs, ordered by finish time, so the next finish is always at the top.

**From PRD §5 Core C functions:**

```c
typedef enum { POL_FCFS, POL_PRIORITY, POL_SJF, POL_AGING,
               POL_AGING_RESERVE, POL_KNAPSACK } PolicyKind;

typedef struct {
    int64_t cpu_cap, mem_cap;
    PolicyKind policy;
    int64_t alpha_milli;        /* aging rate α × 1000, 0..10000 */
    int64_t reserve_threshold;  /* T, ticks */
    double  knapsack_eps;       /* representation open: DECISIONS O-2 */
    int64_t max_jobs;           /* CLI 1,000,000; website 5,000 */
} SimConfig;

typedef struct {
    int32_t id;
    int64_t arrival, duration, cpu, mem;
    int32_t priority;           /* 0..9 */
} Job;

typedef struct Sim Sim;         /* opaque */

int  sim_create(const SimConfig *cfg, Sim **out);
int  sim_add_job(Sim *s, const Job *job);      /* any time, arrival >= now */
int  sim_step(Sim *s);                          /* 1 = event done, 0 = finished */
int  sim_run_until(Sim *s, int64_t t);
int  sim_state_json(const Sim *s, JsonBuf *out);
int  sim_log_json(const Sim *s, int64_t since_seq, JsonBuf *out);
int  sim_results_json(const Sim *s, JsonBuf *out);
int  sim_metrics_json(const Sim *s, JsonBuf *out);
int  sim_reset(Sim *s);                          /* keeps config, clears jobs */
void sim_destroy(Sim *s);

int  exact_solve(const SimConfig *cfg, const Job *jobs, int n, JsonBuf *out);
```

**From PRD §5 Error codes:**

| Code | Name | When | Example message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| -1 | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | Null pointer, bad handle, bad policy | "Unknown policy 9." |
| -2 | `INVALID_FIELD` | A field outside its range (§3); `field` names it | "priority must be 0 to 9." |
| -3 | `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` | Job needs more CPU or memory than the machine has | "Job 4 needs 40960 MB; machine has 32768 MB." |
| -4 | `ARRIVAL_IN_PAST` | Mid-run job with arrival before now | "Arrival 10 is before current time 42." |
| -5 | `DUPLICATE_ID` | Same id added twice | "Job id 3 already exists." |
| -6 | `LIMIT_REACHED` | Too many jobs (§3) | "Website limit is 5000 jobs." |
| -7 | `OUT_OF_MEMORY` | Allocation failed | "Out of memory." |
| -8 | `PARSE_ERROR` | Bad CSV; message gives line and column | "Line 12, column cpu: not a number." |
| -9 | `TOO_LARGE` | Exact solver asked for more than 9 jobs | "Exact solver supports up to 9 jobs." |

**From PRD §6 Input validation:**

- [ ] Every API entry point checks pointers, handles and every field against the ranges in §3 before touching state.
- [ ] A rejected job leaves the simulation unchanged (validate first, then modify).
- [ ] The CSV reader rejects missing headers, extra columns, non-numbers, overflow and lines longer than a fixed limit, reporting line and column.

**From DECISIONS D27, D29 and O-8:**

| # | Decision | Reason | Rejected alternatives | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D27 | `max_jobs` is a field of `SimConfig`: the console program sets 1,000,000, `wasm/api.c` sets 5,000 | The core must know its own limit to return `LIMIT_REACHED` | A compile-time flag per build; an unchecked limit | R1 |
| D29 | Validate first, then modify: a rejected job leaves the simulation unchanged | Predictable errors; no half-applied state | Partial updates | PRD §6 |

| # | Question | Why it matters | Decide in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| O-8 | `REJECT`: does a rejected job get a log entry? Does it appear in `results.csv`? Does the console program stop with exit code 3 or skip the row? (The capacity-rejection golden case depends on it) | API and CSV contract | K-08, K-12 |

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- The opaque `struct Sim` in `engine.c`: config, clock `now`, free CPU/memory, pending arrivals (sorted by arrival, then id), waiting heap, running heap, finished list, job-id set, event log handle, last error
- `sim_create`, `sim_add_job`, `sim_reset`, `sim_destroy`
- Validation of every pointer and every field against PRD §3 before touching state
- Duplicate-id detection, `max_jobs` limit, capacity check, arrival ≥ now
- Deciding O-8 with Krishna and recording it (PRD §5 updated first if the contract changes)

**Out of scope:**

- `sim_step` and the event loop (K-09)
- Event log sentences (K-10)
- JSON outputs (K-11)
- Policies other than storing the config (K-09, K-19)

## 5. Specification

```c
int  sim_create(const SimConfig *cfg, Sim **out);
int  sim_add_job(Sim *s, const Job *job);      /* any time, arrival >= now */
int  sim_reset(Sim *s);                          /* keeps config, clears jobs */
void sim_destroy(Sim *s);
```

Validation order for `sim_create`: `cfg`/`out` non-NULL (else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`); `cpu_cap` 1–1,000,000, `mem_cap` 1–1,000,000,000, `alpha_milli` 0–10,000, `reserve_threshold` 0–1,000,000, `knapsack_eps` 0.01–1, `max_jobs` ≥ 1 (else `INVALID_FIELD` naming the field); unknown `policy` → `INVALID_ARGUMENT` ("Unknown policy 9."). Allocation failure → `OUT_OF_MEMORY` with nothing leaked.

Validation order for `sim_add_job` (all checks before any change, D29):
1. `s`, `job` non-NULL → else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
2. Field ranges (PRD §3): id 0–2,147,483,647; arrival 0–1,000,000,000; duration 1–1,000,000; cpu ≥ 1; mem ≥ 1; priority 0–9 → `INVALID_FIELD` with `field`.
3. cpu > cpu_cap or mem > mem_cap → `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` ("Job 4 needs 40960 MB; machine has 32768 MB.").
4. arrival < now → `ARRIVAL_IN_PAST` ("Arrival 10 is before current time 42.").
5. id already present → `DUPLICATE_ID` ("Job id 3 already exists.").
6. total jobs = max_jobs → `LIMIT_REACHED` ("Website limit is 5000 jobs." / console wording).
7. Insert into pending arrivals; allocation failure → `OUT_OF_MEMORY` with state unchanged.

Each failure stores the error (code, message, field) in the Sim for `aprm_last_error` (K-13). Duplicate-id lookup must be better than O(n) per add (e.g. a sorted id array with binary search or a hash set); state the cost in the comment.

| Test name | What it checks | Expected result |

| `test_create_null` | NULL cfg or out | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` |
| `test_create_bad_field` | cpu_cap 0, alpha_milli 10001, max_jobs 0 | `INVALID_FIELD` naming each field |
| `test_create_bad_policy` | policy = 9 | `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, message "Unknown policy 9." |

| `test_add_past` | Advance now (test hook) then add arrival < now | `ARRIVAL_IN_PAST` |
| `test_reject_unchanged` | Snapshot counts and free resources, add an invalid job | Everything identical after |

## 8. Acceptance criteria (Done when)

- [ ] Each error code returned for its trigger: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `INVALID_FIELD` (with `field`), `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, `ARRIVAL_IN_PAST`, `DUPLICATE_ID`, `LIMIT_REACHED`, `OUT_OF_MEMORY`
- [ ] A rejected job leaves the simulation unchanged (test compares state before and after)
- [ ] Reset keeps the config and clears every job; destroy frees everything (no leaks under `make sanitize`)
- [ ] No global or static mutable state; two Sims can exist at once
- [ ] O-8 decided and recorded; PRD §5 updated first if the contract changed

## 9. How to verify

```sh
make test && make sanitize
```
A pass: every `test_create_*`, `test_add_*`, `test_reset_*` check passes with zero sanitizer reports.

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** the Sim owns all state; functions validate first and modify last, so a bad call can never leave a half-changed simulation.
**Invariant:** pending + waiting + running + finished = total jobs added (PRD §4).
**Complexity:** create O(1); add O(log n) with a sorted pending structure and an O(log n) or O(1) id lookup; destroy O(n).
**Why opaque?** JavaScript and the CLI cannot reach inside, so the core controls every invariant.
**Examiner question:** "What happens if a user adds a job bigger than the machine?" — It is rejected with `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` and the simulation is untouched.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Inserting the job before checking for duplicates (then having to undo)
- O(n) duplicate check per add → O(n²) for a million jobs
- Leaking partially created Sims when a later allocation fails
- Comparing `cpu > cpu_cap` with mixed signed types
